questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of distraction?
questions.explanation: Driving distractions are either physical (reaching for an object), mental (talking with a passenger), or both (using a hand-held phone).

questions.question: Before operating a bus, you should check that the:

options.text: Floor lining is easy to remove.

questions.explanation: When inspecting a bus inside, check that everything is safe and works properly. Make sure emergency exits are clearly marked and easy to use.

questions.question: When should a driver sign a vehicle inspection report?
questions.explanation: Sign a vehicle inspection report only if defects were found and either fixed or confirmed as not needing repair.

questions.question: When you change lanes:

options.text: Other vehicles will likely get out of your way.
You should change lanes slowly and smoothly.
You should wait to change lanes until you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should change lanes slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This keeps your vehicle safe and gives other drivers time to see and react to your movement.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?
questions.explanation: Adjust mirrors before you start driving. If your vehicle has a trailer, the trailer must be straight so you can adjust the mirrors correctly.

questions.question: When a bus stops at an intermediate stop or final destination, passengers should be told:
questions.explanation: When stopping a bus, announce the location, the reason for stopping, the next departure time, and the bus number.

questions.question: Wheel rims that have been welded:

options.text: Should be placed on tires in the rear of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe and should not be used.

questions.question: What should you do to stop an engine fire from spreading?
questions.explanation: Turn the engine off as soon as possible to help stop an engine fire from spreading.

questions.question: If you see taillights ahead while driving in fog:

options.text: The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have pulled off the road.
You can assume the vehicle is on the road.
It may be an optical illusion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is because the vehicle may have pulled off the road.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not a reliable way to find the road. A vehicle's lights may be coming from a car that has left the roadway.

questions.question: When driving in hot weather:

options.text: The air pressure in tires will decrease.
Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.
questions.explanation: In hot weather, check your tire pressure because air expands in heat and increases pressure. To prevent overheating, keep enough oil in the engine and enough water and antifreeze in the cooling system. Antifreeze helps protect your engine in both hot and cold weather.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, what is the safest driving speed?

options.text: Slower than other vehicles around you.
The same speed as other vehicles around you.
Faster than other vehicles around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as other vehicles around you.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles travel in the same direction at the same speed, they cannot crash into each other.

questions.question: A driver talking to passengers should be viewed as:
questions.explanation: Talking to passengers takes a driver's attention away from driving. Use extra caution near drivers who are distracted by conversation.

questions.question: You are unsure if your vehicle will fit safely under a bridge ahead. What should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object, slow down as you approach it. Find an alternate route if possible.

questions.question: Regular vehicle inspections are done to ensure:
questions.explanation: Regular vehicle inspections are most important for safety. They protect you and other drivers on the road.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.
Not having enough oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A faulty exhaust system is a serious safety problem. It can allow poisonous fumes to enter the vehicle's cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: Rims that have been welded for repair:

options.text: Are acceptable only when driving slower than 40 mph.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded for repair are never safe to use.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road.
A thin layer of ice on the road.
Ice that looks black because of dirt on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. The surface looks wet. Watch for black ice if the road looks wet when the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: When parallel parking on the driver's side, you should:

options.text: Drive straight into the parking space.
Back past the space, then drive forward into it.
Drive past the space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on your left. Then back into it. Get your vehicle as close as possible to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: Hydroplaning usually happens:

options.text: Where water builds up on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where water builds up on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs where water has pooled on the road. If there is enough water, hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph. It is more likely if tires are under-inflated or have worn tread.

questions.question: When placing warning triangles on the road, you should:

options.text: Hold the triangles between yourself and oncoming traffic.
Hold the triangles behind your back so other drivers do not see them until they are placed.
Hold the triangles as low as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the triangles between yourself and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: For your safety, carry reflective warning triangles between your body and the oncoming traffic when placing them on the road.
